sources.title: Mend.io upgrades 184 open source organizations to the Renovate Community (OSS) plan
sources.text: Mend.io has proactively upgraded 184 open source organizations and GitHub users to the Mend Renovate Community (OSS) plan, with no request required. The upgrade covers about 3,000 repositories with roughly 4 million combined GitHub stars. Maintainers get higher resource limits, more concurrency, and access to Merge Confidence. At a glance The Community (OSS) plan is a tier of Mend Renovate Cloud, the Mend-hosted version of the Renovate dependency update tool, built for open source maintainers. It gives projects higher resource limits and increased concurrency, so they can keep dependencies up to date without hitting operational bottlenecks. The plan also unlocks Merge Confidence, which is currently only available on the Enterprise plan. Merge Confidence analyzes real-world adoption and test data across the Mend Renovate early-adopter ecosystem to flag releases that may introduce undeclared breaking changes. Together, these features reduce the burden on maintainers and make it easier to keep their software up to date and secure. sources.title: Q3 2026 Open Source Malware Index: When Compromise Compounds
sources.text: Milestone: Since Sonatype began tracking malicious open source packages in 2017, we have logged nearly 2 million malicious packages. Scale: Sonatype Research Labs logged 149,329 open source malware packages in Q3 2026. npm remained overwhelmingly dominant at 89.5% of the quarter's malicious packages, although its share declined from 96.6% in Q2. Behavior: Among packages containing overt-malware behavior, 74.5% involved droppers, secrets exfiltration, or both, showing how often Q3 malware was designed to extend the attack beyond initial execution. Defender challenge: Automation is shortening the distance between initial compromise and follow-on impact, giving defenders less time to contain credential theft, payload delivery, persistence, and further trusted access. In the third quarter of 2026, Sonatype identified 149,329 malicious open source packages across ecosystems, bringing the total logged since tracking began in 2017 to 1,960,846. npm once again accounted for the overwhelming majority this quarter, with 133,579 packages making up 89.5% of the quarter's total. sources.title: TensorLake npm SDK Compromised in ChainDrop Shai-Hulud Credential-Stealing Attack
sources.text: Tensorlake provides isolated sandboxes for running untrusted, LLM-generated code, with checkpointing, suspend, and resume capabilities. Its npm SDK lets developers create and manage those environments from TypeScript applications. A compromised SDK creates exposure on the machine installing it, before generated code reaches a sandbox. The malicious version was published on October 8, 2026, at 01:12:07 UTC. Socket flagged it at 01:23:10 UTC, approximately 11 minutes after publication. The affected release’s published package manifest contains a preinstall hook: "preinstall": "node lib/setup.mjs" Where dependency lifecycle scripts are permitted, this hook gives the malicious loader an execution path during installation. Developers do not need to import the SDK or start an agent for the hook to run. Socket flagged two files in the published package: package/lib/setup.mjs — An obfuscated loader invoked by the preinstall hook that launches the payload using Bun.package/lib/Math_Symbol.js — The obfuscated credential-stealing and self-propagating worm payload. sources.title: AWS Lambda durable functions increases durable operation and checkpoint payload limits
sources.text: Starting today, AWS Lambda durable functions increases the maximum number of durable operations per execution from 3,000 to 30,000, and the maximum checkpoint payload size from 256 KB to 1 MB. Higher operation limits let you safely do more work in a single execution including expanding iterative loops, polling for longer time periods, and building more complex rollback paths that run when a step fails. At 1 MB, checkpoint payloads match the maximum payload size of asynchronous Lambda invocations, and integration services such as Amazon SQS, and Amazon EventBridge, so a workflow can persist a full event from any of these sources in a single operation. AWS Lambda durable functions helps you build resilient multi-step applications and AI workflows that execute for up to one year, with built-in checkpointing, automatic retries, and waits that suspend execution without incurring compute charges. Every durable operation counts toward the per-execution limit, including each step attempt, each poll of a wait-for-condition, and each branch of a parallel or map operation. sources.title: The first disclosure from our Mythos harness
sources.text: It also lists what we didn't test. If we can only prove a narrower claim, we report the narrower claim. Where we're pointing our harness We're focused on the open source that production systems depend on: projects that sit in front of traffic, handle sensitive data, or run inside a lot of other companies' infrastructure. AI serving engines like vLLM are near the top of the list. So far, we've run the harness against over 65 projects and validated over 680 findings. A number of those are in coordinated disclosure now. When a finding holds up, we report it privately to the maintainers, help with the fix where we can, and wait for it to ship. Then we publish an advisory with the maintainers and ship fixed builds to Chainguard customers. We don't publish exploit code. The vLLM bug vLLM is an open source engine that a lot of teams use to serve large language models. In versions before v0.31.0, one client could force the output of other clients on the same engine.
